Synopsis:
    Japan's Finance Minister Katayama and BOJ Governor Ueda will attend the G20 meeting in Asheville, NC, where bilateral talks with US Treasury Secretary Bessent are expected. Markets are focused on yen weakness (159.60/USD, near 40-year lows) following a prior joint US-Japan currency intervention. Bessent has publicly nudged the BOJ toward rate hikes to support the yen. BOJ Deputy Governor Himino reinforced the hawkish tilt without explicitly committing, citing inflation approaching 2%. Markets are pricing an 80–90% probability of a BOJ rate hike in September.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — The article involves the US Treasury Secretary actively engaging on Japan's monetary policy, FX intervention, and G20 macro dynamics, all of which carry cross-market implications for USD, US yields, and global risk sentiment.
